title: The constructible topology of a spectral space is Hausdorff
statement: Let $X$ be a spectral space [def-weil-spectral-space]. Then the set $X$ endowed with its constructible topology [def-weil-pbc-constructible-topology] (the topology with subbase the quasi-compact open subsets of $X$ and their complements) is Hausdorff: for any two points $x\ne y$ of $X$ there are disjoint subsets $A,B\subseteq X$, both open in the constructible topology, with $x\in A$ and $y\in B$.

source.place: Topology, Lemma Tag 0901 (label lemma-constructible-hausdorff-quasi-compact, line 4305), the Hausdorff part (first paragraph of the proof)

proof.text: For distinct points x and y, the T₀ property of a spectral space gives an open set O containing exactly one of them, via `exists_isOpen_xor_mem`. If x is in O, take a compact open U with x ∈ U ⊆ O from the compact-open basis; if y is in O, exchange x and y and make the same choice.

The compact open U is open in the constructible topology by `IsCompact.isOpen_constructibleTopology_of_isOpen`; its complement is open there by `IsCompact.isOpen_constructibleTopology_of_isClosed`, since the complement has compact complement U and is closed in the original topology.

U and its complement are disjoint, and the chosen membership and containment prove that they contain x and y respectively (exchanging the two sets in the second T₀ case). This supplies the pair of disjoint constructible open neighbourhoods required by `T2Space`.

proof_origin.place: The proof follows the Mathlib T₀ separation lemma and compact-open basis, then the constructible subbasis lemmas.
